Initial commit

Declare compatibility with CMake up to 4.1

This silences a warning with newer versions of CMake:

    CMake Deprecation Warning at CMakeLists.txt:1 (cmake_minimum_required):
      Compatibility with CMake < 3.10 will be removed from a future version of
      CMake.

      Update the VERSION argument <min> value.  Or, use the <min>...<max> syntax
      to tell CMake that the project requires at least <min> but has been updated
      to work with policies introduced by <max> or earlier.
Instead of hacky OS detection, have CMake find glut.h

Improve the Array3D interface

This commit replaces get() and set() with call-operator overloads to
enable a shorter, more mathematical programming style.  It also adds
a zero-argument constructor, which is not used in this program but
might be useful to anyone copying the code.
Add a virtual destructor to the virtual Isosurface interface
Fix an ASCII diagram

Use std::size_t from <cstddef>

This is the more C++-style way.
Remove the pointless header comments
Mark OpenGL and GLUT as required dependencies
Implemented copy constructor and operator= for Array3D
Removed trailing whitespace in all files

Switched build system to CMake

This avoids duplication between the XCode project and the Makefile. It also
allows compilation on Windows---assuming you have CMake and OpenGL and GLUT
installed.
Deleted some dead code
Renamed the point and vector types to avoid name clash with std::vector
Added build products to .gitignore
Minor Makefile changes: cleaner syntax and macros for CC/CXX/RM
This code is now licensed under the MIT license
Remove a stray debug line
Add a default implementation for the gradient function of an isosurface that computes a dumb numeric approximation
Fix a whitespace issue
Fix some comments and add a README
Initial commit
Make the demo a little more interesting
Fix rendering for triangles that overlap the top of the screen
Add convenient Material constructors
Fix broken Model copy-constructor
Correctly compute FPS when System.nanoTime() wraps around

Properly convert normals to world coordinates

Previously, triangle normals were in model coordinates but were
compared to world-coordinate vectors, leading to incorrect results.
Fix rotation matrix calculation

Fix a potential array index out-of-bounds

This seems to be due to floating-point imprecision when a triangle is
at an extreme angle very close to the camera plane.  A simple clamp
should mask the issue.

Remove all allocations from the render pipeline

This commit introduces some very non-Java patterns into the code.
While awkward, these patterns ensure that the render pipeline does not
perform any allocations.  With lower GC overhead, performance should be
much more predictable.
Re-use computed triangle normal

Fix hasMotionBlur() calculation

Previously, the condition was always true.

Remove pointless author annotations

Version control does a better job of recording authorship.
Clean up Matrix and fix multiplySelf
Remove definitions and uses of clone()

Camera is not an Object3D

In particular, the scale and rotation are meaningless.  Furthermore,
getMatrix() has entirely different semantics: model matrices convert
from model coordiantes to world coordinates, while camera matrices
convert from world coordinates to camera coordinates.
Clean up and document the World class
Clean up and document ImageProducer
Remove some dead code

Remove WorldEventListener

Rendering is synchronous, so there isn't any need to be informed when
renders complete.

Furthermore, listeners are a fishy programming construct that can
easily put you in callback hell.  Better not to include one unless it's
absolutely necessary.
Correctly implement UVCoord.equals()
Fix an unintentional use of integer division
Move material mode constants to Material class
Use for-each loops instead of uglier syntax
Convert some private members into local variables
Add a docstring to the Camera class
Make a note about external dependencies
Remove the Animator class

Make a small README adjustment

This commit removes a dead link from the README and points people at an
online clone of IDX3D.  It also gives credit to IDX3D's author, Peter
Walser.

Fix rendering when the viewport aspect ratio is not 1:1

Previously, when the viewport width and height were not equal, the
rendered image would be "squashed" to fit the viewport.  This commit
ensures that the world is always rendered correctly, even when the
viewport is not a square.

Fix a bug where some triangles would not render

Previously, if the top two projected vertices of a triangle lay in the
same row, the rendering code would not render that triangle.  This
commit fixes the bug by correctly detecting whether the "B" vertex is
left or right of the "A-C" line.
Implement loading OBJ files with negative face indexes
Converted some member variables into local variables
Redesign ObjImporter and make it thread-safe
Make the Animator class thread-safe
Always generate sources before generating documentation

Renderer is now produced via generated code

This greatly reduces the amount of code to keep track of, and lets me
specify the rendering process in great detail. It is a first step toward
something resembling programmable shaders (but compiled in rather than
built at runtime). It also makes me much more confident that there are
no undiscovered typos in the rendering engine.
Clean up the renderer a little
Move a computation out of an inner loop in the renderer
Use code-generation for some tedious array fill functions
Honor the JAVA and JAVAC make options
Completely empty the demo directory of class files on `make clean`

Minor changes to the demo

 - FPS now only displays to two decimal places
 - App exits when the window is closed

Fix a bug where legal texture coordinates could cause an exception

In short: we were multiplying (u * tex.width) to get an X coordinate
(and doing something similar for Y). This is improper, since the UV
coordinate u can be in the range [0,1] inclusive. We could potentially
try to access the array beyond the end.

The fix is to use (u * (tex.width - 1)) instead.

Improve the demo

The whole "draw at half resolution" thing was a nice pixelated effect
but didn't do a good job of conveying that this engine is any good.

Add a demo to show off a bit
